summary: Moody Tower stood north of Ebro on Highway 79 from the 1960s until a buyer took it down for reuse elsewhere.

facts.status_note: Taken down; the buyer plans to reuse its sections elsewhere.

evidence.supports: north of Ebro on Highway 79; in place since the 1960s
evidence.quote: Located just north of Ebro on highway 79, the tower has been a part of the landscape since the 1960s.

evidence.supports: slow dismantling after decline of fire-watch towers
evidence.quote: By the 1990s, the utilization of fire watch towers had sharply declined

evidence.supports: structures slowly taken down over the years
evidence.quote: resulting in a slow dismantling of the structures over the years
the 2005 decision by then-Governor Jeb Bush to decommission the state’s remaining 35 operational towers

evidence.supports: tower and cottage fell into disrepair; survived storms including Hurricane Michael
evidence.quote: Moody Tower and its caretaker cottage has since fallen into disrepair, yet has remained, standing sentinel over its portion of Washington County, withstanding numerous tropical storms and hurricanes, including Hurricane Michael.

evidence.supports: bought by Mike Vilegi of Excelsior Fire Towers for reuse
evidence.quote: Mike Vilegi, owner of Excelsior Fire Towers, recently purchased the tower and says its legacy will live on, repurposed for use elsewhere.

evidence.supports: top 60 feet with cab headed to Dade City as stargazing tower
evidence.quote: The tower’s top 60 feet, including the cab, is headed down to Dade City, Florida, where it will be used as a stargazing tower.

evidence.supports: lower 40 feet set to go to Tennessee or New Hampshire as a deck
evidence.quote: The lower 40 feet is set to go to either Tennessee or New Hampshire to be used as a wraparound deck for a house being built into a mountain.

evidence.supports: Vilegi and two helpers traveled from New York to take it down
evidence.quote: Vilegi and a crew of two men – Kevin Carter and Jesse Rogers – traveled to Ebro from New York on Tuesday to bring the tower down.

evidence.supports: about six hours with a crane
evidence.quote: Deconstruction of the tower took roughly six hours from start to finish with the help of a crane.
A piece of Washington County history was dismantled Thursday with the deconstruction of the Moody firewatch tower.

evidence.supports: report posted 4 Nov 2021; dismantling reported as Thursday

sources.title: Ebro landscape changes as Moody Tower comes down

notes_for_editor: One news report (Washington County News, republished by MyPanhandle) carries nearly all the history. Correction 2026-10-21: the article is dated 'Posted: Nov 4, 2021' (the 20 Oct 2026 item in the page is a sidebar video, not the article date), so the removal is dated 2021 in events. Build date is only 'since the 1960s'; no builder, height, staffing or fires are in any source. Record status 'unknown' should become 'gone' (facts.status). The article does not say whether the caretaker cottage or footings remain, so the site is undescribed. Destinations of the two sections are stated as plans ('headed', 'set to go'), not confirmed. The 2005 decommissioning was statewide; the article does not say Moody was one of the 35 towers, and the story does not claim it. No agency is named for this tower in these sources, so none is recorded. The record's coordinates fit north of Ebro. No new photos found.

events.note: Report posted 4 Nov 2021 says the tower was dismantled Thursday; the exact day is not stated.
